steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.context: Input: /eval-four-models-without-zebrafish-two-group-n3-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 6 samples, raw integer Salmon gene-level counts, first column gene symbol, Ensembl Danio rerio annotation) and /eval-four-models-without-zebrafish-two-group-n3-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 samples x condition, treated/control). This is a standard two-group unpaired bulk RNA-seq contrast with no batch variable to adjust for.
steps.question: Which genes differ in expression between treated and control zebrafish larvae (3 vs 3, unpaired, single batch)?
acceptance_criteria: DESeqDataSet built with design ~condition, condition releveled so 'control' is the reference level
Genes with near-zero counts across all samples pre-filtered (e.g. rowSums(counts) < 10 removed) before running DESeq()
Wald test contrast extracted as treated vs control with independent filtering (alpha=0.05) and apeglm (or ashr fallback if the coefficient name does not resolve) log2FC shrinkage applied
Output table (all tested genes) contains baseMean, log2FoldChange (shrunk), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj, sorted by padj

Significant DEG lists reported at both padj<0.05 and the relaxed padj<0.1 tier, with counts of both explicitly stated; if very few or zero genes reach padj<0.05, this is stated plainly rather than papered over given n=3/group
QC outputs produced: VST-transformed PCA plot colored by condition, sample-to-sample distance heatmap, and dispersion plot
Volcano plot (EnhancedVolcano) generated from the shrunk results
Background/universe gene list (all genes retained after pre-filtering) exported alongside the DEG lists for downstream enrichment steps

steps.name: Organism-native GO and Reactome pathway enrichment (zebrafish)
steps.context: Uses the DEG table, background gene list, and Wald statistic ranking from T1S1. org.Dr.eg.db (zebrafish OrgDb, Bioconductor, installed) is used for GO ORA/GSEA directly on gene symbols — no ortholog mapping required. Reactome pathway gene sets are staged as a multi-species GMT (ReactomePathways.gmt) with a companion species index (ReactomePathways.txt: stable ID, display name, species); this step must first filter the index to species=='Danio rerio', collect those stable IDs, then subset the GMT to only those IDs before building TERM2GENE/TERM2NAME for clusterProfiler::enricher/GSEA — using the unfiltered multi-species GMT directly would silently mix in human/other-species gene sets.
steps.question: Which GO terms and Reactome pathways are over-represented (ORA) or coordinately shifted (preranked GSEA) among the treated-vs-control DE genes, using zebrafish-native annotation only?
acceptance_criteria: Reactome species index filtered to 'Danio rerio' before subsetting the GMT; the count of zebrafish-specific Reactome pathways found is reported explicitly
If the Danio rerio subset of Reactome is empty or negligible, this is reported and the step relies on GO results only rather than silently proceeding with an unfiltered (wrong-species) gene set

GO ORA (enrichGO, OrgDb=org.Dr.eg.db, keyType matched to the gene symbol identifiers in counts.csv, ont='BP', with the T1S1 background as universe) run on both the padj<0.05 and padj<0.1 DEG tiers from T1S1
GO results de-redundified via clusterProfiler::simplify (GOSemSim) and reported with BH-adjusted p-values
Reactome ORA (clusterProfiler::enricher with the zebrafish-filtered TERM2GENE, same universe) run on the same DEG tiers

Preranked GSEA (fgsea via clusterProfiler::GSEA or gseGO, ranking all background genes by the T1S1 Wald statistic) run for both GO and the zebrafish-filtered Reactome sets, reporting NES and BH-adjusted p-values — included specifically because n=3/group may yield few genes surviving FDR for ORA alone
Output: ranked enrichment tables (ORA and GSEA, GO and Reactome) plus a dotplot or barplot of top terms

steps.name: Supplementary human-ortholog WikiPathways enrichment
steps.context: The reference census confirms WikiPathways gene sets are staged only for human, mouse, and rat (wikipathways_Homo_sapiens.gmt, '%'-delimited header: name, WikiPathways ID, species), not zebrafish. To use it at all requires mapping zebrafish gene symbols to human orthologs first, via the babelgene package (babelgene::orthologs(genes, species='Danio rerio', human=TRUE)), which is staged and supports zebrafish. This step is explicitly supplementary and interpretive, not a primary result, because ortholog mapping loses genes with no confident human ortholog and can introduce one-to-many ambiguity.
steps.question: Via human orthologs, which WikiPathways gene sets are enriched among the treated-vs-control DE genes — as a supplementary cross-species check where zebrafish-native pathway coverage may be sparse?
acceptance_criteria: DEG lists and background from T1S1 mapped to human orthologs via babelgene; the mapping rate (fraction of input zebrafish genes with a resolved human ortholog) is reported explicitly

Where babelgene reports ortholog support/confidence, one-to-one high-confidence orthologs are used preferentially for the primary result, with the all-orthologs result reported separately for comparison
WikiPathways-human GMT parsed by splitting the '%'-delimited descriptor field to recover pathway name and WikiPathways ID before building TERM2GENE/TERM2NAME
ORA (clusterProfiler::enricher) run on mapped DEGs (both padj<0.05 and padj<0.1 tiers) against WikiPathways-human, using the mapped background genes as universe
Preranked GSEA run on the full mapped, Wald-statistic-ranked background against WikiPathways-human

Results are labeled in output as ortholog-based/supplementary and explicitly cross-referenced against the organism-native results from T2S1 — pathways appearing in both are called out as convergent evidence; pathways appearing only here are flagged as ortholog-mapping-dependent

plan.title: Zebrafish drug-exposure DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 6 samples) on the Ensembl Danio rerio annotation, with a single-batch, unpaired 3 treated vs 3 control larvae-pool design. Step 1 runs a standard DESeq2 workflow (QC, dispersion/PCA diagnostics, Wald test treated-vs-control, apeglm LFC shrinkage) to answer 'which genes differ' — explicitly flagging that n=3/group is underpowered for subtle effects and reporting results at both padj<0.05 and a relaxed padj<0.1 tier for transparency. Step 2 answers 'which pathways' using organism-native resources only: GO over-representation via org.Dr.eg.db (installed, offline) and Reactome ORA/GSEA restricted to the Danio rerio subset of the multi-species Reactome GMT (joined via the pathway-ID-to-species index also staged locally) — no ortholog mapping needed since gene symbols already match. Step 3 adds a clearly-labeled supplementary cross-species check: the reference census confirms WikiPathways gene sets exist only for human/mouse/rat, not zebrafish, so this step maps DE genes to human orthologs via babelgene (which covers Danio rerio) before testing WikiPathways-human, with mapping-rate and ambiguity caveats reported alongside results rather than presented as primary findings.
